title: Tarte Tatin
subtitle: Upside-down caramelised apple tart
excerpt: Apples cooked in butter and caramel directly in the pan, covered with shortcrust pastry, baked until the pastry is crisp, then inverted onto a plate so the golden, caramelised apples are on top.

recipe.sourceNotes: Tarte Tatin was created, according to French culinary legend, by the Tatin sisters, Stéphanie and Caroline, who ran a hotel restaurant in Lamotte-Beuvron in the Loire Valley. The story goes that Stéphanie made a standard apple tart in 1898 but accidentally cooked the apples too long in butter and sugar, and attempted to save it by covering the base with pastry and baking it. The upside-down result was so delicious that it became the restaurant's signature dish. It was introduced to Paris by the food writer Curnonsky in the 1930s and from there spread worldwide.

recipeTools.notes: An oven-proof frying pan — essential for making the caramel and then baking.

content.text: The critical moment is the inversion: the tart must be turned out while the caramel is still warm enough to be fluid. If left too long, the caramel will set and the apples will stick to the pan. Place the serving plate on top of the pan, hold both firmly together, and invert in one confident movement. Be careful: hot caramel can cause serious burns.

items.preparation: firm variety such as Braeburn or Cox, peeled, cored, and halved

content.text: Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. In a 25 to 28 cm oven-proof frying pan, melt the butter and sugar together over medium heat without stirring until you have a golden, bubbling caramel, about 6 to 8 minutes.

Arrange the apple halves tightly in the caramel, cut-side up, packing them in as they will shrink during cooking. Cook over medium heat for 10 to 15 minutes until the apples are golden on the base and slightly softened.
Lay the pastry over the apples and tuck the edges down around them inside the pan. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the pastry is golden brown.
Leave to cool in the pan for 5 minutes only. Place a large plate over the pan and quickly invert. Be careful of the hot caramel. Serve warm with double cream or crème fraîche.
